novelty_flags.one_line: The table attributes exact sparse optimization from a polynomial min-cost oracle to Theorem 4.1, but Theorem 4.1 is an equivalence theorem; the stated Algorithm 1 guarantee is Theorem 4.3.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For B with ||B||_{1,2}<=1 and p in (0,1)^n, the paper gives f_B(D) <= (1+epsilon)^2 min{f_B(D_Bernoulli),1+1/epsilon} in time polynomial in m,n,epsilon^{-1}.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 4.1, Theorem 4.1; Theorem 4.3 immediately below Definition 4.2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 4.1 states equivalence of polynomial solvability of MOT, ELLIPSOID, and MIN. Theorem 4.3—not Theorem 4.1—states that Algorithm 1 finds an optimal sparse vertex solution using polynomially many ARGMIN calls.
The paper states that the mixability problem can be solved by dynamic programming in pseudopolynomial time for a fixed number of rows.
The article gives an exact symbolic-homotopy SDP algorithm and states polynomial-time solvability when either the number of scalar variables or matrix size is fixed.
